sources_considered.why: Primary controlled experiments comparing familiar and unfamiliar compositional-task distributions.
Primary experiments on a specific generalization failure across model families.
The pre-post version reports successful length extrapolation and provides material counterevidence to an unrestricted reading.
The default page identifies a December 2024 revision; the May 2024 version was used to preserve the claim's contemporary scope.

evidence_items.explanation: Controlled task splits show sharp degradation outside the trained compositional region. This supports an important instance of the claimed weakness, but does not establish a universal limit across generative AI.

The experiments identify a reproducible failure to reverse learned relations. They support limited generalization in the tested language models, but do not measure a general distance from training examples.

Specially designed embeddings and architectures enable substantial extrapolation beyond trained sequence lengths. This limits any claim that novelty necessarily causes failure, but cannot directly refute an unspecified 'far enough' boundary.

unresolved_gaps: No independently specified meaning of 'far enough' applies across the models and tasks.
The experiments do not represent all generative-AI techniques.
The evidence supports particular failures but does not establish the stronger inevitability claim.
Successful extrapolation does not establish unlimited extrapolation or directly contradict an unspecified failure boundary.
